Het FinOps volwassenheidsmodel: waar sta: The FinOps maturity model: where does your organisation stand?
FinOps is geen project met een einddatum: FinOps is not a project with an end date, but a growth path. The FinOps Foundation describes this path in three phases: Crawl, Walk and Run, where each phase represents a deeper level of cost awareness, automation and collaboration between engineering, finance and business. Most organisations underestimate which phase they are actually in, and that is exactly where savings opportunities remain.
Crawl: zichtbaarheid als startpunt: Crawl: visibility as the starting point
In deze fase is kostendata versnipperd,: In this phase cost data is fragmented, consistent tagging is missing and cost control is reactive, usually only when the invoice arrives. Recognisable by loose spreadsheets, a single dashboard nobody consults structurally, and surprise afterwards at spikes in usage. This is nothing to be ashamed of: almost every organisation starts here.
Hier ontstaat structuur: consistente tag: Here structure emerges: consistent tagging, recurring cost reports per team, and the first steps towards rightsizing and commitment discounts. Teams start to weigh costs in technical decisions, and there is usually a designated owner (or small team) for FinOps within the organisation.
Run: kosten als continu onderdeel van en: Run: costs as a continuous part of engineering
In de volwassenste fase is kostenbewustz: In the most mature phase cost awareness is woven into the way of working: automated anomaly detection, cost allocation that directly influences teams, and architectural decisions that take cost-effectiveness into account right from the drawing board. Saving is then no longer an action, but a property of the system.
{1} Crawl: kostendata is zichtbaar, maar: {1} Crawl: cost data is visible, but fragmented and reactive
{1} Walk: structurele rapportage, eerste: {1} Walk: structural reporting, first optimisations, clear ownership
{1} Run: geautomatiseerd, proactief, ver: {1} Run: automated, proactive, embedded in engineering culture
Belangrijk: je hoeft niet in elke prakti: Important: you don't have to be in the same phase for every practice (cost allocation, optimisation, planning). Most organisations, for example, are far along in visibility but still early in automated optimisation.
Waarom deze indeling praktisch nut heeft: Why this classification is practically useful
Het model voorkomt dat je te snel naar g: The model prevents you from reaching for advanced automation too quickly while the basics (consistent tagging, shared ownership, reliable reporting) are still missing. Conversely, it also prevents mature organisations from getting stuck in manual processes that could have been automated long ago.
De eerste stap is simpel: breng in kaart: The first step is simple: map out which phase you are actually in per practice, instead of going on a feeling. That starting point immediately determines which interventions deliver the most.
